title: THE CALENDAR OF STONE
author: Andries J. Greyling
rationale: HBT Book 1 — ancient-mystery thriller moving from Cape Town up through sub-Saharan Africa. isiZulu applies (KZN/Zulu country, Adam's Calendar in Mpumalanga). Afrikaans applies for SA setting and Cape-origin protagonist milieu. Spanish + French are catalog-wide market languages.

targets.name: isiZulu
directives: Voice: everyday isiZulu as spoken in KwaZulu-Natal — warm, direct, alive. NOT formal SABC/broadcast register, NOT academic-paper Zulu, NOT government-document stiffness.

Do NOT invent pseudo-Zulu transliterations of English words (e.g. ithri-loji, i-derrick). Use established Zulu words or leave English as a natural code-switch — without prefixing every English noun with i-.
Translate into standard isiZulu as written in KwaZulu-Natal, respectful registers throughout.
South African English or Afrikaans words the source uses (bakkie, stoep, veld, kopje, biltong, braai, rooibos, donga, drift) may stay as natural code-switches.
Archaeological / geological / academic terminology (stratigraphy, lithic, assemblage, radiocarbon, artefact) may stay in English where a Zulu academic would use the English term.
Proper names, character names, and invented entities stay verbatim.
Do NOT translate or paraphrase any isiZulu phrases already in the source.

targets.name: Afrikaans
directives: Voice: the people's Afrikaans — contemporary, lived-in, how South Africans actually speak. NOT Hoog-Afrikaans, NOT Netherlands Dutch, NOT archaic Bybel-Afrikaans, NOT newsreader or sermon register. Cape scenes may lean Kaaps where natural; Highveld scenes may lean mine-country speech — always readable, never stiff.
Dialogue and informal narration: natural spoken rhythm, idiomatic turns. Avoid textbook phrases unless a character is deliberately formal.
Natural, contemporary South African Afrikaans (Standaardafrikaans with lived warmth), not Netherlands Dutch and not archaic Bybel-Afrikaans.
South African cultural words already in the source (bakkie, stoep, veld, kopje, biltong, braai, rooibos, donga, drift, highveld) are also Afrikaans — keep them verbatim.
isiZulu or other African-language phrases in the source stay verbatim.
Archaeological / scientific terms may stay in English where that is standard in Afrikaans academic usage.
Proper names, place names, and invented entities stay verbatim.

targets.name: Spanish
directives: Neutral/international Spanish (español neutro) for the widest readership.
ALL South African words stay verbatim and italicised as foreign terms — do not Hispanicise or gloss them.
African-language phrases in the source stay verbatim.
Invented entities and proper names keep their English/source-language form.
Preserve the adventure / discovery pacing — do not over-explain.

targets.name: French
directives: Standard international French.
South African / African-language words stay verbatim, italicised, unglossed.
Invented entities and proper names keep their English/source-language form.
Respect register: field-work scenes vs academic debriefs vs action sequences have different registers.

global_directives: REGISTER: These are novels for real readers, not textbooks or news broadcasts. Regional editions (Afrikaans, isiZulu) must sound like people actually talk — stoep, mine floor, taxi rank — not bulletin or sermon register.

PRESERVE the front-matter structure of build/BOOK.md exactly: title block, copyright page, dedication, epigraphs, chapter order, any back matter. Translate content; keep ORDER and markdown structure byte-for-byte where structural.
The copyright notice, ISBN line, and 'Published by the House of Greyling' stay verbatim — only translate surrounding prose.
Do NOT add translator's notes, footnotes, or bracketed glosses the English source does not contain.
Chapter titles ARE translated unless they are proper nouns.
Output one file per language at build/BOOK.<code>.md, ready for tools/render_book.sh.
